title: Fertilization, pregnancy and early development
blurb: Trace a zygote to a fetus stage by stage, match each germ layer to what it builds, and explain hCG, the placenta, the umbilical vessels and the oxytocin loop of labor.
question: A patient's home pregnancy test turns positive about two weeks after she ovulated. Which hormone did the test detect, which cells made it, and which stage of development has just been completed?

teach.h: From one cell to a fetus
teach.body: Formally, fertilization is the fusion of a sperm with a secondary oocyte, usually in the ampulla of the uterine tube, forming a diploid zygote with 46 chromosomes. Development then runs through cleavage, implantation, the embryonic period (organs form, through week 8) and the fetal period (growth and maturation, week 9 to birth). In plain English: one cell copies itself into a hollow ball, burrows into the uterine lining, builds its organs, then spends months growing.

teach.caption: The inner cell mass becomes the embryo; the trophoblast helps form the placenta. Implantation outside the uterus, usually in the tube, is an ectopic pregnancy.
Note that fertilization happens in the uterine tube; the blastocyst then travels to the uterus and implants in the endometrium.

teach.h: Who decides sex, and how twins arise
teach.body: Enzymes in the sperm's acrosome digest a path to the oocyte. Once a sperm enters, the oocyte finishes meiosis II, and the two haploid sets (23 + 23) combine. Every oocyte carries an X; each sperm carries an X or a Y, so the sperm determines sex (XX female, XY male). Monozygotic (identical) twins come from one zygote that splits. Dizygotic (fraternal) twins come from two oocytes fertilized by two sperm.

head: Hormone
Made by
Job
rows: Keeps corpus luteum alive; pregnancy tests detect it
teach.caption: Without hCG the corpus luteum would degenerate, progesterone would fall and the lining would be shed as a period.

head: Germ layer
Builds
rows: Epidermis of skin; brain, spinal cord and nerves
Lining of digestive and respiratory tracts; liver, pancreas
teach.caption: Hook: ectoderm = exterior and nerves, mesoderm = middle (muscle and bone), endoderm = inner linings.

teach.body: The placenta forms from the trophoblast and the endometrium. Oxygen, nutrients, wastes and IgG antibodies cross between maternal and fetal blood without the two bloodstreams mixing. The placenta is also an endocrine organ that takes over estrogen and progesterone production from the corpus luteum. The amnion wraps the fetus in amniotic fluid, which cushions it. The umbilical cord links fetus and placenta.

teach.caption: Vessel names follow direction (arteries leave the fetal heart), not oxygen content: an exception, like the pulmonary vessels.
The response amplifies the stimulus, so this is positive feedback; delivery ends the loop.

teach.body: Priya ovulated about two weeks ago. A sperm met her secondary oocyte in the ampulla of a uterine tube, forming a zygote. Cleavage made a morula, then a blastocyst, which implanted in her endometrium about a week after fertilization. Its trophoblast now secretes hCG, which keeps her corpus luteum making progesterone, so her lining stays and her period does not come. Her test detected hCG. Over the next weeks her embryo forms its organs.

teach.text: Fertilization happens in the UTERINE TUBE; implantation in the ENDOMETRIUM. The morula is SOLID; the hollow BLASTOCYST implants. hCG comes from the TROPHOBLAST, not the mother's pituitary. Maternal and fetal blood do NOT mix. The umbilical VEIN carries OXYGEN-RICH blood. Embryo through week 8, fetus from week 9. ECTOderm makes the nervous system; ENDOderm makes gut linings. The SPERM sets the sex.

items: Zygote, cleavage, morula, blastocyst, implantation (about a week), embryo (to week 8), fetus (week 9 on).
hCG from the trophoblast keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone; tests detect hCG.
Ectoderm: skin and nerves. Mesoderm: muscle, bone, blood, heart, kidneys. Endoderm: gut and airway linings, liver, pancreas.
Placenta: exchange without mixing; one umbilical vein (oxygen-rich), two arteries (oxygen-poor).
Labor: oxytocin from the posterior pituitary, positive feedback; pregnancy has three trimesters.

summary: You can now put the stages from zygote to fetus in order, say where fertilization and implantation happen, and match each germ layer to the tissues it builds. You can also explain how hCG sustains early pregnancy, how the placenta and umbilical vessels work, and why labor is a positive feedback loop.

A.q: Which sequence correctly orders the earliest stages of human development?
A.why: The zygote divides by cleavage into a solid morula, which becomes a hollow blastocyst; after implantation the inner cell mass develops into the embryo.

whyNot.1: The solid morula comes before the hollow blastocyst, not after it.
whyNot.2: Everything begins with the zygote; the morula is formed from it by cleavage.
whyNot.3: The blastocyst forms and implants before the embryonic period begins.

A.q: Which structure secretes hCG, the hormone detected by home pregnancy tests?
A.why: The trophoblast, the outer layer of the blastocyst (later part of the placenta), secretes hCG, which keeps the corpus luteum producing progesterone.

whyNot.0: The corpus luteum is the target of hCG; it secretes progesterone, not hCG.
whyNot.2: The inner cell mass becomes the embryo itself; it does not secrete hCG.
whyNot.3: The mother's anterior pituitary makes FSH and LH; hCG comes from the embryo's trophoblast.

A.q: Which germ layer forms the lining of the digestive tract?
A.why: Endoderm, the inner germ layer, forms the lining of the digestive and respiratory tracts, the liver and the pancreas.

whyNot.0: Ectoderm forms the epidermis and the nervous system.
whyNot.1: Mesoderm forms muscle, bone, blood, the heart and the kidneys.
whyNot.3: The trophoblast helps form the placenta; it is not a germ layer of the embryo.

B.q: A blastocyst implants in the wall of a uterine tube instead of the uterus. What is this called?
B.why: Implantation outside the uterine cavity, most often in a uterine tube, is an ectopic pregnancy. Normal implantation is in the endometrium.

whyNot.0: Placenta previa is a placenta lying over the cervix inside the uterus, not implantation in the tube.
whyNot.1: Normal implantation takes place in the endometrium of the uterus, not the uterine tube.
whyNot.2: Dizygotic twins come from two fertilized oocytes; twinning says nothing about where implantation occurs.

B.q: Which statement about the umbilical cord is correct?
options: Two arteries carry oxygen-poor blood to the placenta
Two arteries carry oxygen-rich blood to the fetus
One vein carries oxygen-poor blood to the placenta
Two veins carry oxygen-rich blood to the fetus
B.why: The cord has two umbilical arteries, which carry oxygen-poor blood and wastes from the fetus to the placenta, and one umbilical vein, which brings oxygen-rich blood back to the fetus.

whyNot.1: Oxygen-rich blood reaches the fetus through the single umbilical vein, not the arteries.
whyNot.2: The umbilical vein carries oxygen-rich blood toward the fetus, not oxygen-poor blood away from it.
whyNot.3: There is one umbilical vein, not two.

B.q: Why is the embryonic period, through week 8, the time of greatest sensitivity to harmful agents?
options: It gains most of its length and weight then
Its organ systems are forming in these weeks
It has not yet implanted in the endometrium
Its germ layers do not form until week 9
B.why: During the embryonic period the organ systems form, so damage then can disrupt a whole organ. The fetal period that follows is mainly growth and maturation.

whyNot.0: Most growth in length and weight happens in the fetal period, after week 8.
whyNot.2: Implantation happens about a week after fertilization, long before the end of week 8.
whyNot.3: The germ layers form early in the embryonic period, well before week 9.

C.q: A sperm carrying a Y chromosome fertilizes a normal secondary oocyte. What is the chromosome makeup of the zygote?
C.why: Each gamete is haploid (23). The oocyte adds an X and this sperm adds a Y, so the zygote is diploid: 46 chromosomes, XY, a male.

whyNot.0: 23 is the haploid number of one gamete; fertilization restores the diploid number of 46.
whyNot.1: XX would need a sperm carrying an X; this sperm carries a Y.
whyNot.3: An extra chromosome needs an error in meiosis; normal gametes give 46.

C.q: As labor goes on, contractions grow stronger and more frequent until delivery. Which explanation is correct?
options: Rising progesterone makes the myometrium contract harder
Cervical stretch lowers oxytocin, so contractions strengthen
Prolactin from the anterior pituitary drives the contractions
Cervical stretch raises oxytocin, so contractions strengthen
C.why: Stretch of the cervix signals the hypothalamus, the posterior pituitary releases more oxytocin, and the myometrium contracts harder, stretching the cervix further: positive feedback until birth.

whyNot.0: Progesterone relaxes the myometrium; it supports pregnancy rather than driving labor.
whyNot.1: Stretch increases oxytocin release; a fall in oxytocin would weaken contractions.
whyNot.2: Prolactin drives milk production; oxytocin causes uterine contractions.

C.q: A pregnant patient has antibodies against measles. How can these protect her newborn during its first months?
options: Her blood mixes with fetal blood in the placenta
IgG antibodies cross the placenta to fetal blood
Her antibodies diffuse in through amniotic fluid
Her white blood cells cross into the fetal blood
C.why: IgG antibodies cross the placenta from maternal to fetal blood, giving the newborn temporary protection. The two bloodstreams themselves do not mix.

whyNot.0: Maternal and fetal blood do not mix; substances cross the placental barrier between them.
whyNot.2: Amniotic fluid cushions the fetus; it is not the route by which maternal antibodies reach fetal blood.
whyNot.3: The placenta keeps maternal blood cells out of fetal blood; antibodies cross, not white blood cells.

reteach.title: Building a house
reteach.question: Think of building a house from a signed contract to the final coat of paint. How does each stage of the build match a stage of early development?

blocks.body: Fertilization is signing the contract: the full plan (46 chromosomes) is now in one place. Cleavage is making many bricks without enlarging the plot. The blastocyst is the framed shell, and implantation is bolting it to the foundation (the endometrium). The embryonic weeks are plumbing and wiring: mistakes made now are built into the walls. The fetal months are finishing and painting. The placenta is the utility meter: supplies flow in, waste goes out, but the street's pipes never join the house's.

blocks.text: The wiring stage, not the finishing stage, is the risky one: harmful agents do the most damage in the embryonic period, when organs form.

explain.body: Fertilization usually happens in the ampulla of the uterine tube. The acrosome's enzymes let one sperm through; the oocyte then completes meiosis II. Two haploid sets (23 + 23) make a diploid zygote (46). The oocyte always gives an X; the sperm gives X or Y, so the sperm sets the sex.

test.q: Which gamete determines the sex of the child, and which sex chromosome does it supply to a boy?
options: The oocyte; it supplies a Y chromosome
The sperm; it supplies an X chromosome
The oocyte; it supplies an X chromosome
The sperm; it supplies a Y chromosome
test.why: Every oocyte carries an X, so the sex depends on the sperm: an X-bearing sperm gives XX (female) and a Y-bearing sperm gives XY (male). A boy's Y comes from the sperm.

whyNot.0: Oocytes carry an X, never a Y, so the Y of a boy cannot come from the oocyte.
whyNot.1: The sperm is the deciding gamete, but a boy (XY) gets his X from the oocyte; the sperm supplies the Y.
whyNot.2: The oocyte supplies an X to every child, girl or boy, so it cannot be what decides sex.

explain.body: Cleavage divides the zygote into smaller and smaller cells, forming a solid morula. Fluid then opens a cavity, making the blastocyst: an inner cell mass (the future embryo) inside a trophoblast (the future placenta). About a week after fertilization the blastocyst implants in the endometrium, and the trophoblast starts secreting hCG.

test.q: Which statement about the blastocyst is correct?
options: It is a solid ball formed by cleavage
Its inner cell mass becomes the embryo
It normally implants in the uterine tube
Its trophoblast becomes the nervous system
test.why: The blastocyst is hollow; its inner cell mass develops into the embryo and its trophoblast helps form the placenta. It implants in the endometrium.

whyNot.0: The solid ball formed by cleavage is the morula; the blastocyst is hollow.
whyNot.2: Normal implantation is in the endometrium; tubal implantation is an ectopic pregnancy.
whyNot.3: The trophoblast helps form the placenta; the nervous system comes from the ectoderm of the embryo.

explain.body: Early in the embryonic period the inner cell mass forms three germ layers. Ectoderm builds the epidermis and nervous system; mesoderm builds muscle, bone, blood, the heart and kidneys; endoderm builds the linings of the gut and airways, the liver and the pancreas. Organs form through week 8; from week 9 the fetus mostly grows.

items.label: gut and airway linings, liver, pancreas

test.q: The heart, the bones and the kidneys all develop from which germ layer?
test.why: Mesoderm, the middle germ layer, forms muscle, bone, blood, the heart and the kidneys.

whyNot.0: Ectoderm forms the epidermis and the nervous system.
whyNot.1: Endoderm forms the linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts, the liver and the pancreas.
whyNot.3: The trophoblast is not a germ layer; it helps form the placenta.

explain.body: At the placenta, oxygen, nutrients, wastes and IgG cross without maternal and fetal blood mixing. One umbilical vein brings oxygen-rich blood to the fetus; two umbilical arteries return oxygen-poor blood. In labor, cervical stretch triggers oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary, the myometrium contracts harder, and the loop builds until birth.

test.q: During labor, oxytocin is released from which gland, and which tissue does it make contract?
test.why: Oxytocin, made in the hypothalamus, is released from the posterior pituitary and makes the myometrium, the smooth muscle layer of the uterus, contract.

whyNot.0: The myometrium is right, but oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary, not the anterior.
whyNot.1: The posterior pituitary is right, but the endometrium is the lining; the myometrium is the muscle that contracts.
whyNot.2: The placenta makes estrogen and progesterone, not the oxytocin that drives labor contractions.
